metadata.note: The Western Railroad (Western Rail-Road Corporation of Massachusetts, chartered 1833) ran Worcester - Springfield from 1 Oct 1839 and through to Greenbush (East Albany) from Dec 1841, working the Albany and West Stockbridge Railroad in New York as lessee, until it was consolidated with the Boston and Worcester into the Boston and Albany on 4 Sept 1867. This layer draws only the Western's own operating era: the main line in its 1839-1842 opening stages (report blocks [1]-[6], so the map shows it growing west), the 1841-42 temporary route over the Hudson and Berkshire ([5a]) and the Hudson - Chatham branch from 1858 ([8]). One company string and one colour for every feature. Research report: research/branches/western_railroad_of_massachusetts.txt.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-17), routed with opstrace.py: ex-B&A main-line ways tagged old_railway_operator=NYC (Boston Subdivision / Worcester Main Line / Berkshire Subdivision in Massachusetts; Berkshire Subdivision and Post Road Branch in New York).
OSM abandoned ways over the Keystone Arches (Middlefield) for the pre-1912 gorge line; OSM way 281474528, the abandoned 1840 State Line Tunnel bore.

OSM 'Hudson & Berkshire' approximate-location ways (old_railway_operator='Boston & Albany') and OpenHistoricalMap way 202303444 (1835-1860) for [5a]; OpenHistoricalMap way 202268768 (1855-1959) for Claverack - Ghent on [8].

OpenHistoricalMap (2026-10-17) was searched at Worcester, Springfield, the Westfield River gorge, State Line and Greenbush: nothing for the Western's Lower Station, its Springfield depot, the gorge line or the Greenbush depot/ferry landing; those are drawn on the later alignment or at approximate points, as each feature's geometry_quality says.
metadata.operator_split: Every feature ends 1867 (consolidation into the Boston and Albany, 4 Sept 1867, WBA) except [5a], which ends 1842 when the A&WS's own State Line - Chatham section replaced it. The A&WS lease (11 Nov 1841) predates every A&WS train, so no split there. The Hudson branch is drawn as Western only from 1858 (see its note). The Boston and Albany era from 1867 is a separate company and colour and is not drawn here.
omitted: [7] Pittsfield and North Adams (North Adams Branch): NOT drawn here. The Western worked it at least 1857-1866 (its annual reports, AR57-AR66), but data/pittsfield_north_adams_branch.geojson already draws the branch 1846-1870 (pna-pittsfield-north-adams); fixing that layer is out of scope for this change - see existing_layer_note.
[9] Hudson and Berkshire east of Chatham beyond 1842 (Chatham - State Line, the H&B's own trains, 1838 - c.1860): not Western; report drawable NONE.

[10] Connecting roads at Western stations (Hampshire and Hampden, Connecticut River, HN&S, NL&P / NL Northern, Belchertown and Amherst, Stockbridge and Pittsfield, Housatonic, Harlem, Troy and Greenbush, Hudson River, P&W, W&N, N&W): their own trains; report drawable NONE as Western.
Hudson - Chatham 1838-1857 (H&B / Hudson and Boston own or unknown operator): not drawn as Western.
Any Western crossing of the Hudson to Albany in 1866-67: not established; the main line ends at Greenbush.
metadata.existing_layer_note: NOT FIXED HERE (reported only; this change edits no other layer file): (1) boston_and_albany_railroad.geojson, ba-boston-albany 'Boston and Albany: Boston – Albany', draws 1841-1867 in the B&A colour (#5C677D) for years before the B&A existed: west of Worcester those were the Western's trains (this layer), east of Worcester the Boston and Worcester's. With this layer added, Worcester - Albany 1841-1867 is drawn twice (that segment and this layer) until the 1841-1867 segment is removed from ba-boston-albany. Its geometry also crosses the Hudson to the Albany bank for those years, though there was no bridge until 1866, and it carries no geometry_quality. (2) pittsfield_north_adams_branch.geojson, pna-pittsfield-north-adams ('P&NA: Pittsfield - Cheshire - Adams - North Adams', company 'Pittsfield and North Adams Railroad / Western Railroad of Massachusetts', #8C9630) runs 1846-1870: (a) 1867-1870 belongs to the Boston and Albany, which took over the Western's lease on the 4 Sept 1867 consolidation, so ba-north-adams-branch (which starts 1870) should start 1867; (b) for 1857-1867, when the Western's own reports show it worked the branch, the feature should carry company 'Western Railroad' and this layer's colour, with a Rule 6 label such as 'Western Railroad: North Adams Branch'; (c) the 1846-1856 operator (Western vs Housatonic) is unresolved (report UNRESOLVED 1).
not_yet_sourced: All headways and average speeds are estimates. Main-line headways are derived from the in-era train counts the report quotes (Sept 1848 CA48b, Apr 1863 CA63, May 1865 CA65; report UNRESOLVED 9); the [5a] and Hudson branch headways have no count at all. Fisher, 'Whistler's Railroad' (R&LHS Bulletin 69, 1947) was not read.

[5a] the 1841-42 Hudson and Berkshire temporary lease rests on an unidentified 1840s report seen only as a search excerpt; whether the Western ran its own trains over those 15 miles is inferred, not proven (report UNRESOLVED 2). Its alignment is approximate throughout.

[8] Hudson and Boston operator 1855-1870: drawn Western from 1858 on one annual-report sentence (AR58) plus staff movement (CA60); a Western report saying 'worked by the Western' would firm it up (UNRESOLVED 1b). Buyer at the 21 Nov 1854 foreclosure: the Western vs a new Hudson and Boston corporation (UNRESOLVED 4).
Worcester Lower Station location and the Western's pre-1875 Worcester approach (UNRESOLVED 6); the Western's Springfield depot (UNRESOLVED 8); the Greenbush depot and ferry landing (block [6]).

Keystone Arches relocation dated 1912-1913 from a search summary of the NPS article and keystonearches.com (UNRESOLVED 7); other post-1867 line changes between Chester and Dalton, and anywhere else on the main line, were not checked.
Hudson River bridge at Albany: 1866 per another layer's note, not checked; whether Western trains used it in 1866-67 is not established (UNRESOLVED 5).
Mileage conflict on [6]: the report reads FNY as Chatham 177.2 - Greenbush 195.4 (18.2 mi), shorter than the straight-line distance (c.20.9 mi); the true figure is not established.
Second B&A merger date (A&WS and Hudson and Boston): 28 Dec 1870 (WBA) vs 2 Nov 1870 (WHB) - irrelevant to Western years (UNRESOLVED 3).

segments.note: Main line, Eastern Division (report block [1]): Worcester - Rochdale (Clappville) - Charlton - Spencer - East Brookfield - Brookfield - West Brookfield - Warren - Brimfield - Palmer - Wilbraham - Springfield, opened 1 Oct 1839 (WBA, TG; CA39a 'will be open as far as Springfield, by the 1st of October'; CA39b, Gov. Everett's speech at the opening celebration). No earlier 1839 partial opening was found (searched, not disproved). Steam from the first day; no animal power (Rule 5). Through trains from Boston ran over the Boston and Worcester to Worcester (that company's own layer) and the Western beyond. Ends 1867, when the Western was consolidated with the Boston and Worcester into the Boston and Albany (4 Sept 1867, WBA). That is an OPERATOR end, not a passenger end: service continued under the B&A, a separate company and colour not drawn in this layer. Headway is an ESTIMATE derived from in-era train counts the report quotes (UNRESOLVED item 9): Sept 1848 Western timetable, three Boston departures a day through Worcester (CA48b); May 1865, five westbound passenger trains from Worcester plus a freight with passenger car (CA65). About four trains over an 18-hour day is c.270 min; not a sourced headway for any one year.

properties.geometry_quality: Drawn 12.9 mi against '15 miles' documented (the unnamed 1840s report quoted in block [5a]; -14%). ENTIRE FEATURE IS APPROXIMATE: the Hudson and Berkshire east of Chatham was abandoned c.1860 and no track survives. Pieces used: 1.4 mi of OSM way 1326324979 ('approx. loc Hudson & Berkshire (abandoned @1860)', State Line - Canaan) and 2.1 mi of OSM way 407840898 ('Hudson & Berkshire'), both tagged old_railway_operator='Boston & Albany' and fixme='Approximate location'; then 5.6 mi of an untagged OpenHistoricalMap railway way dated 1835-1860 (OHM 202303444) towards Chatham, which agrees with the OSM approximate pieces where they overlap. STRAIGHT-LINE LEGS (approximated): 1.56 mi between the two OSM approximate ways near Canaan; 2.25 mi from the end of the OHM way north-east of Chatham to Chatham Four Corners (CA55b says the H&B and the Western ran 'side by side for several miles' here and crossed, so the true line lay close to the A&WS track); plus joins of 0.02 and 0.08 mi. The Chatham end is the same point as the A&WS features' Chatham junction. Treat the whole alignment as indicative, not surveyed.

segments.note: Temporary route (report block [5a], MEDIUM-LOW confidence). From the Greenbush opening in Dec 1841 until the Albany and West Stockbridge's own State Line - Chatham section opened on 12 Sept 1842 (WBA), Western through trains ran the 15 miles between the state line and Chatham Four Corners over the Hudson and Berkshire Railroad under a temporary lease. The lease and its end in 'the summer of 1842' rest on a quotation from an unidentified 1840s railroad report that the researcher saw only as a search-result excerpt (the host returned 503) - NOT READ IN FULL; that the Western rather than the H&B ran the trains is INFERRED from the word 'lease' and from a Western locomotive reaching Greenbush (CA41), not stated. The H&B east of Chatham was otherwise the H&B's own road (not drawn) and was abandoned c.1860. Drawn 1841-1842 at year resolution, overlapping in 1842 the A&WS feature that replaced it. Headway is an UNSOURCED estimate (no 1841-42 train count found; two through trains a day assumed by analogy with Sept 1848, CA48b).

Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Albany and West Stockbridge Railroad, western section (report block [6]): Chatham Four Corners - Chatham Centre - Kinderhook (Niverville) - Schodack (Brookview) - East Greenbush - Greenbush (East Albany, today's Rensselaer). Opened 21 Dec 1841 (WBA); an Albany paper reported the Western's locomotive 'puffing and blowing into Greenbush' and the first passenger train for Boston leaving the next morning (CA41). Worked by the Western as lessee from opening (lease of 11 Nov 1841, WBA). Greenbush was the Western's terminal - passengers crossed to Albany by ferry (CA42 'railroad depot in Greenbush'; CA48b 1848 'trains for Troy leave on the arrival of the trains at Greenbush'). No Hudson bridge existed at Albany until 1866, and whether Western trains crossed it in 1866-67 is not established, so the feature stops on the east bank for the whole span. Ends 1867, when the Western was consolidated with the Boston and Worcester into the Boston and Albany (4 Sept 1867, WBA). That is an OPERATOR end, not a passenger end: service continued under the B&A, a separate company and colour not drawn in this layer. Headway is an ESTIMATE derived from in-era train counts the report quotes (UNRESOLVED item 9): two through trains a day each way west of Springfield in Sept 1848 (CA48b: 8 a.m. from Boston arriving Albany 6.30 p.m.; Albany departures 7 a.m. and 2.30 p.m.) and three west from Springfield in Apr 1863 (CA63). About 2.5 trains over an 18-hour day is c.420 min; not a sourced headway for any one year.

The Hudson end is on the riverfront track near the H&B's river landing; the landing's exact site is approximate. Whether the 1838 H&B line differed from the later B&A branch anywhere was not checked; the drawn line is the B&A-era branch.

segments.note: Hudson and Berkshire / Hudson and Boston, Hudson - Claverack - Mellenville - Ghent - Chatham Four Corners (report block [8], MEDIUM-LOW confidence for the operator). Built and run by the Hudson and Berkshire from 1838 (its own trains; not drawn as Western). Bought at foreclosure 21 Nov 1854 (CA54a; to the Western per WHB and CA54b), renamed Hudson and Boston 23 Feb 1855 (WHB). In Aug-Sept 1855 it still ran its own trains (CA55a, CA55b), so 1855-1857 is passenger service of unknown operator and is NOT drawn as Western. Drawn from 1858 because the Western's report for 1858 counts its receipts 'from all sources (including those of the Hudson and Boston road)' (AR58), and a former Western brakeman became a Hudson and Boston conductor in 1860 (CA60) - no source says 'worked by the Western' in so many words. Passenger trains are attested in the era (CA56 1856, CA59 1859). Ends 1867 with the Western; the B&A ran it afterwards (formally merged 1870). Headway is an UNSOURCED estimate - the report found no train count for this branch.
